name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q01 - Milestones in early experiments on photosynthesis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding early experiments in photosynthesis:

(I) Joseph Priestley hypothesised that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove.
(II) Jan Ingenhousz showed that in the dark, small bubbles were formed around the green parts of an aquatic plant, while in bright sunlight they did not.
(III) Julius von Sachs provided evidence that glucose is produced when plants grow and is usually stored as starch.
(IV) T.W. Engelmann used a prism to split light and observed that aerobic bacteria accumulated mainly in the green and yellow regions of the split spectrum.
(V) Cornelius van Niel inferred that the \(\text{O}_2\) evolved by green plants comes from \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), not from carbon dioxide.

How many of the given statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding Priestley's hypothesis
Joseph Priestley observed that a burning candle or a breathing mouse fouled the air in a closed bell jar, whereas introducing a mint plant allowed the mouse to survive and the candle to burn. From this, he hypothesised that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding Ingenhousz's aquatic plant experiment
Jan Ingenhousz demonstrated that in bright sunlight, small bubbles were formed around the green parts of an aquatic plant, whereas in the dark, these bubbles did not form. These bubbles were later identified as oxygen. The claim that bubbles formed in the dark rather than in sunlight reverses the experimental findings, making this statement inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding Julius von Sachs's findings
Julius von Sachs showed in 1854 that the green substance in plants is located in special bodies (later termed chloroplasts) where glucose is made, and that this glucose is usually stored in the form of starch. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding Engelmann's experiment
T.W. Engelmann split light using a prism and illuminated the green alga Cladophora in a suspension of aerobic bacteria. He observed that the bacteria congregated primarily in the regions of blue and red light of the spectrum where oxygen evolution was greatest, not in the green and yellow regions. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding Cornelius van Niel's formulation
Based on his studies of purple and green sulfur bacteria, Cornelius van Niel demonstrated that photosynthesis is a light-dependent reaction where hydrogen from an oxidisable substrate reduces carbon dioxide. Because sulfur or sulfate is produced when \(\text{H}_2\text{S}\) is used instead of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\), he concluded that the oxygen released by green plants originates from water and not from carbon dioxide. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
Counting the valid evaluations confirms that the findings related to Priestley, Sachs, and van Niel are scientifically correct, while those related to Ingenhousz and Engelmann are incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: Exactly three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q02 - Organization and absorption spectra of photosynthetic pigments

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements concerning photosynthetic pigments and light harvesting complexes:

(I) A chromatographic separation of leaf pigments reveals that chlorophyll a appears bright or blue-green, whereas chlorophyll b appears yellow-green.
(II) Accessory pigments such as chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids enable a wider range of wavelengths of light to be utilised and protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.
(III) The light harvesting complex (LHC) within each photosystem is made up of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins, including the single reaction centre chlorophyll a molecule.
(IV) In Photosystem I, the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at \(700\text{ nm}\), whereas in Photosystem II it absorbs maximally at \(680\text{ nm}\).
(V) The action spectrum of photosynthesis shows an absolute, complete one-to-one overlap with the absorption spectrum of chlorophyll a across all wavelengths.

Which of the following combinations contains all the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding chromatographic separation of leaf pigments
Paper chromatography demonstrates that leaf colour is due to four pigments: chlorophyll a (bright or blue-green), chlorophyll b (yellow-green), xanthophylls (yellow), and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding the role of accessory pigments
Accessory pigments (chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids) absorb light at wavelengths other than those absorbed by chlorophyll a and transfer that energy to the reaction centre. They also shield chlorophyll a from damage caused by photo-oxidation. Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding light harvesting complex organisation
Each photosystem possesses hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins that form the antenna or light harvesting complex; however, this complex excludes the single chlorophyll a molecule that specifically constitutes the reaction centre. Therefore, asserting that the antenna includes the reaction centre molecule is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding reaction centre absorption peaks
In Photosystem I (PS I), the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption maximum at \(700\text{ nm}\) (designated \(\text{P}_{700}\)), whereas in Photosystem II (PS II), it absorbs maximally at \(680\text{ nm}\) (designated \(\text{P}_{680}\)). Hence, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding spectrum overlap
Although the action spectrum of photosynthesis shows prominent peaks in the blue and red regions matching chlorophyll a, there is not a complete one-to-one overlap because accessory pigments also absorb light at intermediate wavelengths. Hence, claiming an absolute one-to-one overlap is inaccurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The evaluations confirm that the statements concerning leaf pigment colors, accessory pigment functions, and photosystem absorption peaks are correct.
Final Conceptual Answer: The combination comprising statements (I), (II), and (IV) only represents the valid set.

questiontext.text:
Examine the following five statements regarding cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation:

(I) In non-cyclic electron transport, electrons excited from PS II pass downhill along a redox potential scale through an electron transport system of cytochromes to PS I.
(II) The water-splitting complex is physically associated with PS II and is located on the outer surface of the thylakoid membrane facing the stroma.
(III) Stroma lamellae membranes possess PS I but lack PS II as well as the \(\text{NADP}\) reductase enzyme.
(IV) Cyclic photophosphorylation results in the synthesis of both \(\text{ATP}\) and \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\).
(V) Cyclic electron flow occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond \(680\text{ nm}\) is available for excitation.

How many of the given statements are INCORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding electron transport from PS II to PS I
In non-cyclic photophosphorylation, light absorption at \(680\text{ nm}\) excites electrons in PS II, which are accepted by an electron acceptor and passed downhill through an electron transport chain containing cytochromes to PS I. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding the location of the water-splitting complex
The water-splitting complex is associated with PS II, which is physically located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane facing the lumen. Because protons and oxygen are released into the lumen and not onto the stroma-facing outer surface, placing it on the outer side is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding stroma lamellae composition
While granal thylakoid membranes contain both PS I and PS II, the stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II and \(\text{NADP}\) reductase, retaining only PS I. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding cyclic photophosphorylation products
In cyclic photophosphorylation, excited electrons cycle back to the PS I reaction centre through the electron transport chain without moving to \(\text{NADP}^+\). Consequently, cyclic photophosphorylation produces only \(\text{ATP}\) and does not generate \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\). Thus, claiming both are produced is inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding wavelength requirements for cyclic flow
When wavelengths beyond \(680\text{ nm}\) illuminate the chloroplast, PS II is not effectively excited, leaving only PS I operational. Under these conditions, cyclic electron flow and photophosphorylation take place. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
Among the five statements, two statements—the one describing the location of the water-splitting complex and the one asserting that cyclic photophosphorylation synthesises \(\text{NADPH}\)—are incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: Exactly two statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q04 - Mechanism of chemiosmotic ATP synthesis in chloroplasts

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the chemiosmotic hypothesis in chloroplasts:

(I) Protons produced by the photolysis of water accumulate in the thylakoid lumen, resulting in a measurable decrease in lumen \(\text{pH}\).
(II) The primary electron acceptor from PS II transfers its electron to a hydrogen carrier, which removes a proton from the stroma and releases it into the lumen.
(III) The enzyme \(\text{NADP}\) reductase is located on the lumen side of the thylakoid membrane and releases protons into the lumen.
(IV) The \(\text{CF}_0\) component of \(\text{ATP}\) synthase is embedded in the thylakoid membrane and forms a transmembrane channel for facilitated diffusion of protons.
(V) Movement of protons through \(\text{CF}_0\) occurs from the stroma into the lumen, activating the catalytic \(\text{CF}_1\) particle on the lumen side.

Which of the following combinations includes all the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding photolysis and lumen proton accumulation
Water photolysis occurs on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane, directly dumping protons into the thylakoid lumen. This proton build-up increases proton concentration and lowers lumen \(\text{pH}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding the hydrogen carrier
The primary electron acceptor of PS II is located towards the outer side of the membrane and passes its electron to an \(\text{H}\) carrier (plastoquinone). This molecule picks up a proton from the stroma; when it transfers its electron to an inner electron carrier, it discharges the proton into the lumen. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding NADP reductase orientation
The \(\text{NADP}\) reductase enzyme is located on the stroma side of the thylakoid membrane. It extracts protons from the stroma along with electrons from PS I to reduce \(\text{NADP}^+\) to \(\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+\), thereby depleting stroma protons rather than releasing them into the lumen. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding the structure and role of CF0
\(\text{ATP}\) synthase consists of \(\text{CF}_0\), an integral transmembrane channel embedded within the thylakoid membrane that facilitates proton diffusion across the membrane, and \(\text{CF}_1\), which protrudes into the stroma. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding proton direction during ATP generation
Protons flow down the electrochemical gradient from the lumen back into the stroma through the \(\text{CF}_0\) channel. This flow drives a conformational shift in the \(\text{CF}_1\) unit facing the stroma to produce \(\text{ATP}\). Stating that protons move from stroma to lumen reverses the established direction. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The statements detailing water photolysis, hydrogen-carrier mediated proton pumping, and \(\text{CF}_0\) transmembrane architecture are correct.
Final Conceptual Answer: The combination comprising statements (I), (II), and (IV) only represents the correct set.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PHOTOSYNTHESIS_IN_HIGHER_PLANTS_STATEMENT_Q05 - Energetics and stages of the Calvin cycle

questiontext.text:
Read the following statements regarding the Calvin cycle (\(\text{C}_3\) pathway):

(I) Carboxylation is the most crucial step of the cycle, in which \(\text{CO}_2\) is fixed by ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (\(\text{RuBP}\)) to form two molecules of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (\(\text{3-PGA}\)).
(II) The reduction stage involves the utilisation of \(2\) molecules of \(\text{ATP}\) for phosphorylation and \(2\) molecules of \(\text{NADPH}\) for reduction per \(\text{CO}_2\) molecule fixed.
(III) For the net synthesis of one molecule of glucose, \(6\) turns of the cycle are required, consuming a net total of \(12\text{ ATP}\) and \(12\text{ NADPH}\).
(IV) Regeneration of the primary \(\text{CO}_2\) acceptor \(\text{RuBP}\) requires the expenditure of two molecules of \(\text{ATP}\) per \(\text{RuBP}\) regenerated.
(V) The Calvin cycle operates in all photosynthetic plants, irrespective of whether they possess \(\text{C}_3\) or \(\text{C}_4\) pathways.

How many of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding carboxylation
Carboxylation is the fixation of \(\text{CO}_2\) into a stable intermediate. In this step, \(\text{CO}_2\) combines with the 5-carbon ketose sugar \(\text{RuBP}\), catalysed by \(\text{RuBisCO}\), to produce two molecules of 3-carbon \(\text{3-PGA}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding reduction requirements per CO2 fixed
During the reduction stage, each fixed \(\text{CO}_2\) molecule requires \(2\) molecules of \(\text{ATP}\) for phosphorylation and \(2\) molecules of \(\text{NADPH}\) for reduction to form triose phosphates. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding overall energetic inputs for one glucose molecule
To produce one molecule of glucose (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\)), \(6\) molecules of \(\text{CO}_2\) must be fixed through \(6\) turns of the cycle. Across the whole cycle, this requires \(18\text{ ATP}\) (\(12\text{ ATP}\) in reduction plus \(6\text{ ATP}\) in regeneration) and \(12\text{ NADPH}\), not \(12\text{ ATP}\). Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding ATP requirement during regeneration
The regeneration of the \(\text{CO}_2\) acceptor molecule \(\text{RuBP}\) requires one molecule of \(\text{ATP}\) for phosphorylation per turn of the cycle, not two. Thus, this statement is inaccurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding occurrence of the Calvin cycle in all photosynthetic plants
The Calvin pathway is the universal biosynthetic pathway for sugar formation in all photosynthetic plants, taking place in the mesophyll cells of \(\text{C}_3\) plants and in the bundle sheath cells of \(\text{C}_4\) plants. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The statements regarding carboxylation, per-\(\text{CO}_2\) reduction stoichiometry, and universal occurrence are scientifically valid, whereas the overall \(\text{ATP}\) count for glucose synthesis and the regeneration stoichiometry are invalid.
Final Conceptual Answer: Exactly three statements are correct.

questiontext.text:
Examine the following statements regarding the \(\text{C}_4\) pathway and photorespiration:

(I) Bundle sheath cells in \(\text{C}_4\) leaves are characterised by having thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, no intercellular spaces, and a large number of chloroplasts.
(II) In the mesophyll cells of \(\text{C}_4\) plants, primary \(\text{CO}_2\) fixation is catalysed by \(\text{RuBisCO}\), forming oxaloacetic acid.
(III) In bundle sheath cells, \(\text{C}_4\) acids are decarboxylated to release \(\text{CO}_2\), which raises the intracellular concentration of \(\text{CO}_2\) and suppresses the oxygenase activity of \(\text{RuBisCO}\).
(IV) In the photorespiratory pathway of \(\text{C}_3\) plants, \(\text{RuBisCO}\) binds \(\text{O}_2\) to convert \(\text{RuBP}\) into one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate, with neither synthesis of sugars nor of \(\text{ATP}\).
(V) \(\text{C}_4\) plants exhibit saturation of photosynthesis at lower atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) concentrations (about \(360\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\)) than \(\text{C}_3\) plants (which saturate beyond \(450\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\)).

Which of the following combinations contains all the correct statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the statement regarding Kranz bundle sheath anatomy
Kranz anatomy in \(\text{C}_4\) plants is characterised by bundle sheath cells arranged in several layers around vascular bundles. These cells possess thick walls that are impervious to gas exchange, lack intercellular spaces, and contain abundant chloroplasts. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the statement regarding mesophyll carboxylation enzymes
In \(\text{C}_4\) plants, primary carboxylation occurs in the mesophyll cells where phosphoenolpyruvate (\(\text{PEP}\)) fixes \(\text{HCO}_3^-\) via the enzyme \(\text{PEP}\) carboxylase (\(\text{PEPcase}\)). The mesophyll cells lack \(\text{RuBisCO}\). Thus, attributing primary fixation here to \(\text{RuBisCO}\) is inaccurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the statement regarding bundle sheath decarboxylation
Malic acid or aspartic acid transported from mesophyll cells is broken down in bundle sheath cells through decarboxylation, releasing \(\text{CO}_2\) and a 3-carbon acid. This mechanism enriches \(\text{CO}_2\) around \(\text{RuBisCO}\), ensuring it functions almost exclusively as a carboxylase and preventing photorespiration. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the statement regarding the photorespiratory reaction
When \(\text{RuBisCO}\) binds \(\text{O}_2\) in \(\text{C}_3\) plants, \(\text{RuBP}\) is cleaved into one molecule of 3-carbon phosphoglycerate and one molecule of 2-carbon phosphoglycolate. The pathway releases \(\text{CO}_2\) with consumption of \(\text{ATP}\), yielding neither \(\text{ATP}\) nor sugars. Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the statement regarding CO2 saturation thresholds
Under high light intensities, \(\text{C}_4\) plants attain photosynthetic saturation at approximately \(360\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\) of \(\text{CO}_2\), whereas \(\text{C}_3\) plants saturate only above \(450\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\). Thus, this statement is accurate.

Step 6: Check and Final Conceptual Conclusion
The evaluations confirm that the statements describing Kranz anatomy, bundle sheath decarboxylation, photorespiratory stoichiometry, and \(\text{CO}_2\) saturation levels are scientifically valid, while the statement attributing mesophyll fixation to \(\text{RuBisCO}\) is incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: The combination comprising statements (I), (III), (IV), and (V) only represents the valid set.
